title: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit

circuit.name: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit

components.label: 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V

activities.title: 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This is where power enters the bench. Follow the line, neutral and earth from here.

activities.title: Electricity meter
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: A supply meter records energy in kilowatt-hours. Its practice display shows the power passing through its own line connection right now, in kilowatts (kW).

activities.title: Main switch
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: One handle disconnects both line and neutral.

activities.title: Distribution board
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: Open the door to reach the breakers. Behind the front panel are the rails, wires and terminal bars.

activities.title: Lamp circuit breaker (MCB)
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: A circuit breaker trips if too much current flows. A heavy fault can trip it quickly. A smaller overload can take longer.

activities.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: The lamp gets brighter as it draws more power. Measure from L to N to check the voltage across it.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: Switch off the main switch. Will the lamp stay on?
activities.explanation: The meter records how much electricity you use. Turning off the main switch cuts power to the board. The wires feeding the switch can still be live.
activities.clue: Find the main switch. Follow the wire on each side. Which side goes to the lamp?

options.label: It goes out
It stays on while the meter has power

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Electricity meter · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Electricity meter · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Electricity meter · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Electricity meter · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · LOUT to Main switch · LIN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · LOUT to Main switch · LIN with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Load side of the meter. Follow L through to LIN. Incoming L terminal. Follow it to LOUT on the other side of the same pole.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · NOUT to Main switch · NIN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · NOUT to Main switch · NIN with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Load side of the meter. Follow N through to NIN. Incoming neutral terminal. Follow it to NOUT on the other side of the same pole.

activities.title: Connect Main switch · LOUT to Distribution board · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Main switch · LOUT to Distribution board · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal. Follow it to LIN on the other side of the same pole. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Main switch · NOUT to Distribution board · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Main switch · NOUT to Distribution board · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing neutral terminal. Follow it to NIN on the other side of the same pole. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · PEOUT to Distribution board · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · PEOUT to Distribution board · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · LOUT to Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · LOUT to Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal. Follow it to LIN on the other side of the same pole. Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · NOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · NOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing neutral terminal. Follow it to NIN on the other side of the same pole. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · PEOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · PEOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Check the lamp with the main switch on
activities.instruction: Check the lamp with the main switch on.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power

activities.title: Turn the main switch off
activities.instruction: Turn the main switch off.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit stops drawing power

activities.title: Turn the main switch back on
activities.instruction: Turn the main switch back on.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Lamp on the outgoing circuit, put red on L and black on N. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Compare line to neutral before and after the main switch. With that switch open, its supply side can still read close to mains voltage.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 and Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Which device turned off the supply to the board?
activities.explanation: The meter records how much electricity you use. Turning off the main switch cuts power to the board. The wires feeding the switch can still be live.
activities.clue: Find the main switch. Follow the wire on each side. Which side goes to the lamp?

options.label: The meter
The main switch

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit
challenge.briefing: The meter has power and the outgoing breaker is on. The lamp stays dark.
challenge.firstCheck: The lamp breaker is on. Does voltage reach the lamp as well as the meter?
challenge.hint: Start at the outgoing breaker. Compare its output with the line terminal at the lamp.
challenge.answer: The line wire from the breaker to L on the lamp is broken.

activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This device compares the current in line and neutral. If some returns another way, it can trip. A separate breaker or fuse protects against overload.

activities.title: Outgoing MCB 2

activities.explanation: A circuit breaker trips if too much current flows. A heavy fault can trip it quickly. A smaller overload can take longer.

activities.title: Socket on breaker 2
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: A double socket with an appliance plugged into the circuit. Both earth terminals share one metal strap.

No, the socket stays on

options.label: Its own breaker and the RCCB are both still on
The lamp breaker switches only the neutral

challenge.title: Find the fault · Shared RCCB with outgoing MCB circuits
challenge.briefing: The lamp has gone out and the socket has lost power too.
challenge.firstCheck: Check the lamp and the socket. Which switch on the board supplies both?
challenge.hint: Check which device tripped. Read its trip record and compare the current going out with the current coming back.
challenge.answer: Current from the lamp circuit is leaking to earth. The shared RCCB has opened, so both circuits lose power.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Measure across each lamp
activities.instruction: Measure across each lamp.
activities.explanation: Hall light A draws power. Hall light B draws power. Hall light C draws power. All three lamps have nearly the same voltage.

expectedObservations.title: All three lamps have nearly the same voltage

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Hall light A, put red on L and black on N. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Read L to N at each lit lamp. Each should be close to the full supply. The shared feed carries the current for all the lamps that are on.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load and Hall light B · N. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Trace the two wires at each lamp. Where do they go?
activities.explanation: Each lamp has its own path from the switched line to neutral. Electricians call that a parallel circuit.
activities.clue: Pick a lamp. Follow both of its wires. Does either wire have to pass through another lamp?

options.label: Back to the same switched line and neutral
From one lamp through the next, in a chain

activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Parallel lighting bank
challenge.briefing: One lamp is dark. The two beside it still work.
challenge.firstCheck: Leave the lamps switched on. Start at the dark lamp and compare it with a lit one.
challenge.hint: Compare the dark lamp’s line and neutral connections with the working lamps.
challenge.answer: The neutral to lamp B is broken. The other two lamps still have a way back through neutral.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Ring final circuit with a fused branch
challenge.briefing: The heater is off. The sockets on the ring still work.
challenge.firstCheck: The fuse has opened. Look at the trip record for the current it carried just beforehand.
challenge.hint: Look at the fuse rating, then read the current it carried just before it opened. There’s no current in the heater wire now.
challenge.answer: The heater drew more than the branch fuse’s 3 A rating, so the fuse opened. The ring sockets are on the other side of it.

activities.title: Try the sink setting
activities.instruction: Try the sink setting.
activities.explanation: Short element · sink mode draws power. Long element · bath mode stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Short element · sink mode draws power
Long element · bath mode stops drawing power

activities.title: Switch to Bath
activities.instruction: Switch to Bath.

expectedObservations.title: Short element · sink mode stops drawing power
Long element · bath mode draws power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Short element · sink mode, put red on L and black on N. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Measure across each element with its thermostat calling. The selected branch should have close to the supply voltage, while the other is off.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Sink / bath element selector · A and Sink element thermostat · COM. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

options.label: The bath element’s thermostat

activities.title: Repair the fault

challenge.answer: The wire from selector A to the Sink thermostat is broken. Bath has a separate feed.

activities.title: Turn down the thermostat in room A
activities.instruction: Turn down the thermostat in room A.
activities.explanation: Manifold actuator A opens. Manifold actuator B closes. Manifold circulation pump draws power.

activities.title: Turn down the other room thermostat
activities.instruction: Turn down the other room thermostat.
activities.explanation: Manifold circulation pump stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Manifold circulation pump stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Manifold circulation pump, put red on L and black on N. Record the reading.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Room A demand · OUT and Underfloor heating wiring centre · I1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: When should the shared pump stop in this circuit?
activities.explanation: Each room has its own valve actuator, the part that moves the valve. The pump keeps water moving while either room still needs heat.
activities.clue: Turn down one room thermostat. Check the other room’s valve before looking at the pump.

options.label: When neither room calls for heat
As soon as either room reaches temperature

challenge.title: Find the fault · Water underfloor wiring centre and actuators
challenge.briefing: Room A is cold but its valve stays shut. Room B can still run the pump.
challenge.firstCheck: Ask for heat in room A only. Check the valve for that room before looking at the shared pump.
challenge.hint: Compare the signal leaving room A’s thermostat with input I1 at the wiring centre.
challenge.answer: The wire from thermostat A to I1 is broken. The wiring centre still gets room B’s signal.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Simple switched extractor fan
challenge.briefing: The fan switch is on but the fan does not run.
challenge.firstCheck: With the wall switch on, measure across L and N at the fan.
challenge.hint: Trace the fan’s neutral back to the outgoing neutral terminal.
challenge.answer: The neutral wire to the fan is broken. Its switch can still supply line, but no current can flow through the fan.

activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. The metal strap joins both earth terminals. Either terminal connects to the same earth path.

activities.title: Turn on the bench and local supplies
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply. Choose Grid-following PV inverter · AC side and turn it on with Operate.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity. Solar and battery supplies have their own controls.

activities.title: Check grid power with the solar panels generating
activities.instruction: Check grid power with the solar panels generating.
activities.explanation: Now try the next setting.

activities.title: Try the same load with no sunlight
activities.instruction: Try the same load with no sunlight. Choose Test circuit to compare the two settings.
activities.explanation: With the panels shaded, the house takes more power from the grid.

expectedObservations.title: With the panels shaded, the house takes more power from the grid

activities.title: Switch off the grid supply
activities.instruction: Switch off the grid supply.
activities.explanation: The inverter detects the loss of mains. House socket stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: The inverter detects the loss of mains

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On House socket, put red on L and black on N. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Read signed power at the grid connection. The change includes both the house demand and the inverter contribution. This circuit represents the AC side of the inverter.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Inverter AC isolation · LOUT and Grid-following PV inverter · AC side · L. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why did the grid reading change if the same appliances stayed on?
activities.explanation: Shade the panels and leave the appliances on. Watch the grid meter. As the panels supply less power, the house draws more from the grid.
activities.clue: Leave the appliances on. Compare the grid power with the panels in sunlight and again with them shaded.

options.label: The appliances now need more power to do the same job
The house takes more from the grid when the panels give less

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Solar inverter and its AC connection
challenge.briefing: The panels are in full sun, but the house is taking all its power from the grid.
challenge.firstCheck: Set the panels to full sunlight. Check the house load and the grid reading.
challenge.hint: With the AC isolator on, check L and N at the inverter. Compare that with the outgoing side of the isolator.
challenge.answer: The line between the AC isolator and inverter is broken. The house still has grid power.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

challenge.title: Find the fault · Three-phase DOL motor starter
challenge.briefing: The motor starts, then stops as soon as you lift your finger.
challenge.firstCheck: Hold Start down. Can the starter keep the motor running once you let go?
challenge.hint: Follow the starter’s auxiliary output 14 back to coil A1.
challenge.answer: The link from 14 to A1 is broken. Start supplies the coil while you hold it. When you let go, the coil drops out.

activities.instruction: Press Start, then let go. Watch the star contactor drop out and the delta contactor pull in.
activities.explanation: Star contactor · mechanical pair opens. Delta contactor · mechanical pair closes. Six-terminal motor · 400 V delta / 690 V star draws power. Each motor winding is rated for 400 V.

Each motor winding is rated for 400 V

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Six-terminal motor · 400 V delta / 690 V star, put red on U1 and black on U2. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Watch the star contactor when you press Start. After the delay, watch it drop out and delta pull in. The bench shows the winding connections. It leaves out the brief rush of starting current.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Transition changeover contact · NO and Star contactor · mechanical pair · 21. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why does the starter release star before closing delta?
activities.explanation: Star joins three winding ends together. Delta joins the windings end to end. The timer opens the star contactor before it closes delta.
activities.clue: Follow the motor connections with star closed. What would the delta contacts join if they closed too soon?

challenge.title: Find the fault · Six-terminal star-delta motor starter
challenge.briefing: The motor starts in star. Star drops out when the timer finishes, but delta never pulls in.
challenge.firstCheck: Start the motor and wait for the timer. Watch the star and delta contactors in turn.
challenge.hint: Trace the timer relay’s NO contact to the star contactor. What should feed the delta coil once star drops out?
challenge.answer: The wire from the timer relay’s NO contact to terminal 21 on the star contactor is broken. The delta coil gets no feed at changeover.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

challenge.title: Find the fault · Motor control from two stations
challenge.briefing: Neither Start button works, even with both Stop buttons released.
challenge.firstCheck: Try Start at each station. Which parts of the Stop circuit do both stations share?
challenge.hint: Trace the wire from NC on the Stop button at B to terminal 95 on the overload.
challenge.answer: The wire from Stop B to overload terminal 95 is broken. Both Start buttons have lost their feed.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Sequential two-motor conveyor control
challenge.briefing: The receiving belt runs. The feed belt won’t start.
challenge.firstCheck: Start the receiving belt first. Leave it running while you try the feed belt.
challenge.hint: Follow the wire from 14 on the receiving belt starter to Stop on the feed belt.
challenge.answer: The wire from terminal 14 on the receiving starter to the feed belt’s Stop button is broken. The second starter never gets the signal that the first belt is running.

activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Pump B starter · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Pump B starter · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Pump B starter · A2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Pump B starter · A2 with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Try pump A first
activities.instruction: Try pump A first.
activities.explanation: Pump A runs. Pump B stays off.

activities.title: Select pump B
activities.instruction: Select pump B.
activities.explanation: Pump A stops. Pump B runs on its own.

expectedObservations.title: Pump B runs on its own

activities.title: Lift the high-level float
activities.instruction: Lift the high-level float.
activities.explanation: Pump A runs with the float up. Pump B runs with the float up.

expectedObservations.title: Pump A runs with the float up
Pump B runs with the float up

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Three-phase motor · externally linked star, put red on U1 and black on U2. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Check each pump coil with the float down, then up. If a pump runs only with the float up, follow the wire from the duty selector.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Duty selection A / B · A and Pump A control junction · 1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: The selector is marked Duty. What does it choose?
activities.explanation: The duty selector picks the first pump. A separate float calls the second pump when one is no longer enough.
activities.clue: Choose the first pump. Raise the high-level float and watch the other pump.

options.label: Which pump runs first
Whether both pumps run together

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Duty/standby pumps and high-level assist
challenge.briefing: Select pump A with the high-level float down. A stays off, but B runs when you select it.
challenge.firstCheck: Leave the high-level float down. Try A on its own, then B on its own.
challenge.hint: Check A at the duty selector and the wire leading to pump A’s control junction.
challenge.answer: The wire from selector A to pump A’s junction is broken. The high-level float can still start both pumps.

components.label: Motor overload and NC control contact

activities.title: 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: The three line terminals are L1, L2 and L3. At the 400 V setting, expect about 230 V from any one of them to neutral.

activities.title: Three-pole circuit breaker
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: One handle switches all three phases. If a fault trips one pole, all three open together.

activities.title: PLC-commanded starter
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: A small coil pulls the main contacts closed to feed a larger load. Extra contacts can hold the coil on or signal that it has closed.

activities.title: Motor overload and NC control contact
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: If the motor draws too much current, the overload opens its small switch marked 95–96. In the starter circuit, that cuts power to the coil and stops the motor.

activities.title: Three-phase motor · externally linked star
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: There are two ends to each of the three windings. The links between these six terminals set the motor for star or delta.

activities.title: Isolated 24 V control supply
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This takes the incoming supply and gives the controls their own DC supply. Measure across + and − to check it.

activities.title: PLC · 24 V controller
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This controller reads signals from the switches and sensors. Its program decides which outputs turn on.

activities.title: Workpiece-present sensor
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: The sensor needs its own supply. When it detects the change it is set for, it switches its output on.

activities.title: Machine-ready permission
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: The sensor needs its own supply. When it detects the change it is set for, it switches its output on.

activities.title: Controller status light · Q2
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This small panel light comes on when there is enough voltage across its terminals.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: The part is in place, but the machine-ready signal is off. Will the starter pull in?
activities.explanation: Trace the two sensor wires to I1 and I2 on the PLC. Both inputs have to be on before its output Q1 can start the motor.
activities.clue: Leave one input off. Try the other and watch Q1, the controller’s output.

options.label: No, it needs both signals
Yes, either signal will do

activities.title: Connect PLC-commanded starter · 4 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 3
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join PLC-commanded starter · 4 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 3 with the phase L2 wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of the main contacts 3–4. When the coil pulls in, these two terminals join and can carry the load current. Incoming side of 3–4. The overload checks motor current here. If it trips, 95–96 open. In the starter lesson that cuts power to the coil.

activities.title: Connect PLC-commanded starter · 6 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 5
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join PLC-commanded starter · 6 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 5 with the phase L3 wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of the main contacts 5–6. When the coil pulls in, these two terminals join and can carry the load current. Incoming side of 5–6. The overload checks motor current here. If it trips, 95–96 open. In the starter lesson that cuts power to the coil.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 2 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 2 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 with the phase L1 wire.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 4 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · V1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 4 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · V1 with the phase L2 wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of 3–4. The overload checks motor current here. If it trips, 95–96 open. In the starter lesson that cuts power to the coil. V winding start, paired with V2. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 6 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · W1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 6 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · W1 with the phase L3 wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of 5–6. The overload checks motor current here. If it trips, 95–96 open. In the starter lesson that cuts power to the coil. W winding start, paired with W2. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · PE

activities.explanation: U winding end, paired with U1. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta. V winding end, paired with V1. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta.

activities.title: Connect Three-phase motor · externally linked star · V2 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · W2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Three-phase motor · externally linked star · V2 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · W2 with the output wire.
activities.explanation: V winding end, paired with V1. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta. W winding end, paired with W1. Measure between these ends to see what voltage this winding receives with the links in star or delta.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Three-pole circuit breaker · 2 to Isolated 24 V control supply · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries phase 1 out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Isolated 24 V control supply · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Isolated 24 V control supply · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Isolated 24 V control supply · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Isolated 24 V control supply · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to PLC · 24 V controller · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to PLC · 24 V controller · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Power for the controls. Check the voltage on this unit. These lessons use 24 V.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to PLC · 24 V controller · N

activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Return for the control supply. Measure from L to N to check the supply voltage.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to PLC · 24 V controller · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to PLC · 24 V controller · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Feed for the output contacts. The controller has its own power supply. COM needs a feed of its own.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Workpiece-present sensor · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Workpiece-present sensor · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Workpiece-present sensor · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Workpiece-present sensor · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Machine-ready permission · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Machine-ready permission · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Machine-ready permission · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Workpiece-present sensor · IN with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Control input. Measure from IN to N to see whether the control signal reaches this fitting.

activities.explanation: Switched output. When the control operates, it connects L to OUT. This output uses the same supply as the fitting. Wired input. Measure I1 to N to check the signal. This controller reads it as on above half its control voltage.

activities.title: Connect Machine-ready permission · OUT to PLC · 24 V controller · I2

activities.explanation: Switched output. When the control operates, it connects L to OUT. This output uses the same supply as the fitting. Wired input. Measure I2 to N to check the signal. This controller reads it as on above half its control voltage.

activities.title: Connect PLC · 24 V controller · Q1 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95

activities.explanation: Q1 passes the feed from COM when the contact closes. The program decides when Q1 closes. Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to PLC-commanded starter · A2

activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect PLC · 24 V controller · Q2 to Controller status light · Q2 · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join PLC · 24 V controller · Q2 to Controller status light · Q2 · L with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Q2 passes the feed from COM when the contact closes. Q2 follows input I2. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Controller status light · Q2 · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Controller status light · Q2 · N with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Controller status light · Q2 · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Controller status light · Q2 · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.instruction: Give the controller both start signals.

activities.explanation: Check the control supply, both input voltages, output COM and the coil circuit. Power at the PLC electronics alone cannot show that Q1 has a supply to switch.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Workpiece-present sensor · OUT and PLC · 24 V controller · I1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: The controller uses an AND rule. What does that mean for these two inputs?
activities.explanation: Trace the two sensor wires to I1 and I2 on the PLC. Both inputs have to be on before its output Q1 can start the motor.
activities.clue: Leave one input off. Try the other and watch Q1, the controller’s output.

activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.

challenge.title: Find the fault · PLC inputs and motor starter
challenge.briefing: Both sensors are on, but the PLC won’t start the motor.
challenge.firstCheck: Leave both sensors on. Which of the two inputs lights up on the PLC?
challenge.hint: Compare the signal leaving the presence sensor with I1 at the controller.
challenge.answer: The wire from the part sensor to I1 is broken. The PLC sees only one of the two signals it needs.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Safety relay · COM with the control wire.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Safety input channel A · NC · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Safety input channel A · NC · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Safety input channel B · NC · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Safety input channel B · NC · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Safety input channel A · NC · NC to Safety relay · S1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Safety input channel A · NC · NC to Safety relay · S1 with the control wire.

activities.title: Connect Safety input channel B · NC · NC to Safety relay · S2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Safety input channel B · NC · NC to Safety relay · S2 with the control wire.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Machine motor contactor · 21
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · + to Machine motor contactor · 21 with the control wire.

activities.title: Connect Machine motor contactor · 22 to Safety relay · FB
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Machine motor contactor · 22 to Safety relay · FB with the control wire.

activities.title: Connect Safety relay · OUT to Stop · NC · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Safety relay · OUT to Stop · NC · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Switched feed from COM. Opening a safety input cuts this feed. Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Stop · NC · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95

activities.explanation: Normally closed. NC joins COM at rest. It opens while you hold the button down. Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Start · NO · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Start · NO · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Machine motor contactor · 13
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Machine motor contactor · 13 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go.

activities.title: Connect Start · NO · NO to Machine motor contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Start · NO · NO to Machine motor contactor · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open. NO joins COM while you hold the button down. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Machine motor contactor · 14 to Machine motor contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Machine motor contactor · 14 to Machine motor contactor · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Machine motor contactor · A2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Machine motor contactor · A2 with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.instruction: On Three-phase motor · externally linked star, put red on U1 and black on U2. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Press Reset with the motor stopped. Look at the relay and measure across the starter coil. Does Reset alone start the motor?

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Machine motor contactor · 22 and Safety relay · FB. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: What did Reset do in this circuit?
activities.explanation: A small contact tells the safety relay when the motor contactor has let go. Once the safety circuit is ready, Reset allows a fresh start. The motor waits until you press Start.
activities.clue: Press Reset and leave Start alone. Watch the motor before you touch another button.

options.label: It let the machine accept a fresh press on Start
It started the motor on its own

challenge.title: Find the fault · Safety relay and contactor feedback
challenge.briefing: Both safety inputs are closed. You press Reset, but the starter still won’t accept Start.
challenge.firstCheck: Leave the motor stopped and press Reset. Check the two safety inputs and the feedback input.
challenge.hint: With the motor stopped, follow the wire from 22 on the contactor to FB on the safety relay.
challenge.answer: The wire to FB is broken. The safety relay can’t tell that the contactor has let go, so it won’t reset.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Light a cupboard when its door opens

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply

activities.title: Turn the left worktop switch off
activities.instruction: Turn the left worktop switch off.

activities.title: Turn the left switch back on and the right switch off
activities.instruction: Turn the left switch back on and the right switch off.
activities.explanation: left strip draws power. right strip stops drawing power.

activities.instruction: On left strip, put red on +24 V and black on −. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Measure between the two pads on each strip. The lit strip should have about 24 V across it.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between right worktop switch · 1 and right strip · +24 V. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why does the right strip stay on?
activities.explanation: The two branches share the driver. Each switch controls only the strip connected to it.

The left strip still carries the right strip’s current

challenge.title: Find the fault · Light each worktop separately
challenge.briefing: Both switches are on. The left strip lights up. The right one stays dark.
challenge.firstCheck: Start at the strip that stays dark. Both worktops use the same driver.
challenge.hint: Put black on the right strip’s − pad and red on its + pad. Leave black there and move red to the wire leaving the right switch.
challenge.answer: There’s a break between the right switch and its strip. The left worktop still works because it uses a separate branch.

activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This is where power enters the bench. Follow the line, neutral and earth from here.

activities.title: Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This breaker protects one circuit. It can trip on too much current or when some current returns by another path.

activities.title: 350 mA constant-current driver
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: This driver adjusts its output voltage to keep the current through the LEDs steady, within its working range. Check the current rating on the driver.

activities.title: First series module
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: These LEDs are wired one after the other. The same current flows through every module in a complete string.

activities.title: Second series module
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: These LEDs are wired one after the other. The same current flows through every module in a complete string.

activities.title: Removable series link
activities.instruction: Choose Show terminals. Pick one of the marked points where the wires go.
activities.explanation: The rocker joins two contacts to turn the lamp on. Flick it back and the contacts open.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: You open the link between the downlights. Which one stays lit?
activities.explanation: The same current passes through both downlights. A break anywhere in that loop puts both lights out.
activities.clue: Open the link between the two downlights. Look at both lights.

options.label: The downlight nearest the driver
Neither downlight

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. Top N takes the neutral feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked N.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 350 mA constant-current driver · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 350 mA constant-current driver · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 350 mA constant-current driver · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 350 mA constant-current driver · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom N carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked N. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to 350 mA constant-current driver · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to 350 mA constant-current driver · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect 350 mA constant-current driver · + to First series module · +
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 350 mA constant-current driver · + to First series module · + with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Positive LED input on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Connect First series module · − to Removable series link · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join First series module · − to Removable series link · COM with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative LED return on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver. Common terminal. The feed comes in here in the lighting lesson. The rocker joins COM to L1.

activities.title: Connect Removable series link · L1 to Second series module · +
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Removable series link · L1 to Second series module · + with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: In the lighting lesson this wire goes to the lamp. Switching off breaks its connection to COM. Positive LED input on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Connect Second series module · − to 350 mA constant-current driver · -
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Second series module · − to 350 mA constant-current driver · - with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative LED return on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver. Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Take a reading with both LEDs on
activities.instruction: Take a reading with both LEDs on.
activities.explanation: First series module draws power. Second series module draws power. The same current flows through both LEDs. The meter reads about 9 V across the first LED.

expectedObservations.title: The same current flows through both LEDs
The meter reads about 9 V across the first LED

activities.title: Open the series link
activities.instruction: Open the series link.
activities.explanation: First series module stops drawing power. Second series module stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: First series module stops drawing power
Second series module stops drawing power

activities.title: Close the link to light both LEDs again
activities.instruction: Close the link to light both LEDs again.
activities.explanation: First series module draws power. Second series module draws power.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On First series module, put red on + and black on −. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: With 350 mA flowing, the meter reads about 9 V across each light and about 18 V across the pair. Open the link and the current falls to zero. The voltage across the driver rises towards its limit.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Removable series link · L1 and Second series module · +. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why do you read more volts across the driver than across either downlight?
activities.explanation: The same current passes through both downlights. A break anywhere in that loop puts both lights out.
activities.clue: Close the link again. Measure each downlight on its own, then measure across the driver.

options.label: The driver supplies the voltage for both lights in series
The second downlight takes twice the current

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Find out why two downlights go out together
challenge.briefing: Neither downlight lights up even with the link closed.
challenge.firstCheck: Close the link. Both downlights share one path. Look between them as well as at the driver.
challenge.hint: Turn off the bench supply. Check the wire from the removable link to the second downlight.
challenge.answer: The wire between the link and the second downlight is broken. The lights are in series, so current has to pass through both.

challenge.briefing: Press the front button and the bell rings. Press the back button and it stays quiet.

activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. Top N takes the neutral feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked N.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 24 V isolated DC driver · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 24 V isolated DC driver · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 24 V isolated DC driver · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 24 V isolated DC driver · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom N carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked N. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to 24 V isolated DC driver · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to 24 V isolated DC driver · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Call button · Top screw
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Call button · Top screw with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Either wire can go here. Press the button and the top and bottom screws are connected.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Call light timer · 4 s · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Call light timer · 4 s · L with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Call light timer · 4 s · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Call light timer · 4 s · N with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Call button · Bottom screw to Call light timer · 4 s · IN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Call button · Bottom screw to Call light timer · 4 s · IN with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Either wire can go here. Press the button and the top and bottom screws are connected. Control input. Measure from IN to N to see whether the control signal reaches this fitting.

activities.title: Connect Call light timer · 4 s · OUT to Call beacon · +24 V
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Call light timer · 4 s · OUT to Call beacon · +24 V with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Switched output. When the control operates, it connects L to OUT. This output uses the same supply as the fitting. The positive wire meets the copper pad marked +24 V here.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Call beacon · −
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Call beacon · − with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. The negative wire returns to the driver from this pad marked −.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Press the call button
activities.instruction: Keep Call button pressed while you check this step.
activities.explanation: Call beacon draws power.

activities.title: Let go and watch the light
activities.instruction: Let go and watch the light.
activities.explanation: Call beacon draws power.

activities.title: Wait four seconds and check the light
activities.instruction: Wait four seconds and check the light.
activities.explanation: Call beacon stops drawing power.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: On Call beacon, put red on +24 V and black on −. Record the reading.
activities.explanation: Measure across the light just after release and again once it goes out. When the timer finishes you should see about 0 V across the light.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Call light timer · 4 s · OUT and Call beacon · +24 V. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: You’ve let go of the button. What’s still feeding the light?
activities.explanation: The push starts the timer. The timer’s own supply keeps the light on after the visitor lifts their finger.
activities.clue: After you let go of the button, follow the light’s feed back to the timer. Which terminal does it reach?

options.label: Current passing through the open push
The timer’s OUT terminal

activities.title: Repair the fault

activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Find the fault · Keep a light on after you let go
challenge.briefing: The timer starts when you press the bell button, but the call light stays dark.
challenge.firstCheck: Hold the call button while you check. Does the timer operate even if the light stays dark?
challenge.hint: Watch the timer when you press the push. Compare the timer output with voltage across the call light.
challenge.answer: The wire from timer OUT to the light is broken. The timer runs, but the light gets no feed.

The valve stays where it stopped

activities.title: Switch the valve control back on
activities.instruction: Switch the valve control back on.
activities.explanation: The valve is fully closed.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

options.label: CLOSE and COM
OPEN and COM

challenge.title: Find the fault · Move a valve and stop it halfway
challenge.briefing: The valve opens. Choose Close and it stays where it is.
challenge.firstCheck: Open the valve first. Leave movement enabled, then select Close.

challenge.answer: There’s a break between B on the selector and CLOSE on the valve. The wire to OPEN is still sound, so the valve can travel one way.
